data.title: fix(governance): drop a quarterly budget's quarter start when a single-budget update moves it to another window
data.body:
## Summary

A deprecated single-budget update (`budget: {...}`) that moves a quarterly budget to another window no longer fails with a 500.

`BudgetsFromSingleBudgetUpdate` merges the request into the stored budget and keeps every field the request does not name, including `reset_config` (the quarter start). When the request changes `reset_duration` from `1Q` to, say, `1M` without naming `reset_config`, the kept quarter start rode along onto a window it is invalid for, `validateBudget` refused it ("reset_config is only valid on a quarterly reset duration"), and the route answered 500.

- The kept quarter start is dropped when the final window is not quarterly and the request did not send its own `reset_config`.
- A request that names `reset_config` is applied as sent, unchanged.

Affects every route that still accepts the single `budget` field: customer updates, and a business unit's update in builds that offer business units.

## Repro (before)

1. A customer with a `1Q` budget and `reset_config: {quarter_start_month: 4}`.
2. `PUT /api/governance/customers/{id}` with `{"budget": {"reset_duration": "1M"}}` returns 500 "Failed to update customer".

## Tests

- `TestBudgetsFromSingleBudgetUpdateKeepsResetConfig` (new case: moving off the quarterly window drops the quarter start)
- `TestUpdateCustomer_LegacyBudgetLeavesTheQuarterBehind` (returns 500 without the fix, 200 with it)

data.title: refactor(governance): export the owned-budget reconciler for other builds
data.body:
## Summary

Exports the budget reconciler so a build whose owners live outside this package gets the same rules a team or customer does.

- `ReconcileOwnedBudgets` is the one path that upserts an owner's budgets: matched by id or by reset window, usage carried on a matched row, inherited from the closest shorter window on a new one, removed rows deleted, and the operator's usage reset applied and reported. The customer and model-config reconcilers now wrap it, so a field added there is carried for every owner.
- `BudgetUsageReset` (with `NewBudgetUsageReset` / `BudgetIDs`), `ValidateRateLimit`, `IsBudgetRemovalRequest` and `IsBadRequestError` are exported alongside it, and the deprecated single-budget conversion is exported under a name that says what it returns: `coerceLegacyBudget` becomes `BudgetsFromSingleBudgetUpdate` (one function, no wrapper; its tests renamed to match).

No behaviour change for existing routes; the wrappers keep the same bodies. `ReconcileOwnedBudgets` refuses a nil transaction with an error: the store reads an explicit nil as a transaction it was given and would dereference it, and the budget writes must commit with the owner's row anyway. The customer test mock now hands its callback a placeholder transaction, as a real store never passes nil.

## Tests

- `TestReconcileOwnedBudgets`, `TestReconcileOwnedBudgetsRefusesBadDeclarations`, `TestReconcileOwnedBudgetsRefusesANilTransaction`
- `transports/bifrost-http/handlers` suite passes on this branch alone.

data.title: feat(ui): let a downstream build say what governs an entity's spend
data.body:
## Overview

Lets a downstream build say what already governs a team, business unit or customer's spend, and has the customer sheet ask before offering the entity's own limit fields.

- `lib/registries/entityGovernance`: a runtime registry for a probe hook, with a default that reports nothing governing the entity. A downstream build registers its probe by importing a module through the `@enterprise` alias. The OSS build gets a no-op fallback module under `_fallbacks`.
- The probe reports what governs the entity (`governedBy`), whether the answer is still loading, and whether the check failed, with an optional `retry`.
- The customer sheet offers its budget and rate-limit fields to every ungoverned customer, in every build. A governed customer gets the name field only, since a write of limits to it would be refused.
  - New customers and customers that already hold limits of their own skip the probe.
  - While the probe is loading, the fields stay hidden, so limits are never offered to a customer that turns out to be governed.
  - If the check fails, the fields stay hidden and the sheet says why, with a retry button. An unknown answer is not treated as "nothing governs it".
  - Limit validation only runs while the fields are offered, so renaming a governed customer isn't blocked by hidden values.
  - Previously the enterprise build hid the fields from any customer that had none, including new ones.
- Adds the `customers.sheet.limitsCheckFailed` message to all locales (de, en, es, fr, it, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh-CN, zh-TW).

## Tests

- `lib/registries/entityGovernance.test.ts` covers:
  - the default answer when no probe is registered
  - arguments being passed through to a registered probe
  - a failed check and its retry being passed through unchanged
  - reset returning to the default

data.title: feat(databricks): configurable OAuth M2M scopes
data.body:
## Summary

A user setting up Databricks with a service principal hit this on every request:

```
oauth token request to https://dbc-....cloud.databricks.com/oidc/v1/token failed (403): access_denied Scopes 'all-apis' are not assigned to the client [redacted]; the client has scope(s) [all-apis:read] that cannot send this request
```

Databricks now lets an admin limit an OAuth secret to specific scopes when creating it, and the scopes can't be changed afterwards. A token minted from a scoped secret can't exceed those scopes, and the token endpoint refuses any request naming a scope the secret lacks. Bifrost hardcoded `scope=all-apis`, so every scoped secret failed at the mint.

This adds `databricks_key_config.scopes`. When it's empty the key requests `all-apis` as before, so no existing key changes. When it's set, Bifrost sends exactly those scopes, space-joined. `all-apis:read` alone still can't run inference, because querying a serving endpoint is a POST. The docs say so and point to `model-serving-inference`.

## Changes

- `core/schemas/account.go`: `Scopes` on `DatabricksKeyConfig`. `OAuthConfig` uses it, falling back to the shared `all-apis` slice. `ValidateScopes` refuses a blank entry or one containing whitespace, since `"a b"` would quietly request two scopes.
- `framework/configstore`: new `databricks_scopes` text column (space-joined) with migration `add_databricks_scopes_column`. The migration bounds the Postgres lock wait at 5s, like `add_oauth_key_config_columns`. Scopes are carried through `Redacted()` so a UI edit doesn't drop them.
- `transports/bifrost-http/handlers/provider_keys.go`: key validation calls `ValidateScopes`.
- UI: a Scopes tag input on the Databricks OAuth M2M tab. It splits a pasted "a b" into two tags and is cleared when switching to PAT. There's a new `databricksScopesHelp` string in all 11 locales.
- `transports/config.schema.json`, `helm-charts/bifrost/values.schema.json`: the `scopes` property.
- Docs: an "OAuth scopes" section in `providers/supported-providers/databricks.mdx` that maps scopes to features, a troubleshooting row for the 403, and a note in the config-json guide. Model listing needs no scope, because Bifrost lists Databricks models from its catalog and never calls the workspace for them.

## Cost on the request path

No new allocations. `OAuthConfig` runs per request and returns either the key's own slice or the shared default, with no copying. The token cache key already hashed `Scopes`, so keys that differ only in scopes get separate cached tokens. That entry is the same size and lifetime as today's one entry per credential. I didn't add a benchmark because the change is a slice selection with nothing new to measure. The existing `oauth_internal_test.go` benchmark covers the path.

## Tests

- `core/providers/databricks/oauth_internal_test.go`: `TestOAuthM2M` now runs the default case and a scoped key whose token request has to carry exactly its scopes.
- `core/providers/utils/tokencache/oauthkey_test.go`: configured scopes replace the default, keys that differ only in scopes have different cache keys, and scope validation.
- `framework/configstore/tables/key_databricks_test.go`: scopes round-trip in order, and clearing them falls back to the default.
- `transports/bifrost-http/handlers/provider_keys_databricks_test.go`: the redacted-merge round trip keeps scopes, and validation accepts scoped keys and rejects blank or whitespace-joined scopes.

Red before green: with `OAuthConfig` temporarily put back to the hardcoded slice, the new cases fail on assertions (`scope: got "all-apis", want "model-serving-inference model-serving"`) and pass with the fix. The `framework/configstore` migration suite passes. I didn't run `make test-core PROVIDER=databricks` because I had no Databricks credentials in that checkout.

## Provider harness

There's a new preview case in folder 208, `databricks oauth scopes`. `databricks-token-fixture.mjs` gains a host, `dbx-scoped-workspace.invalid`, that behaves like a secret scoped to `model-serving-inference`. It answers a request for any other scope with Databricks' 403 `access_denied`, and it mints and serves a chat reply for the right scope. The case first checks that saving a whitespace-joined scope gets a 400, then expects a 200 from the scoped key. Before this change it fails with the 403, because Bifrost asks for `all-apis`. The existing 401 host is unchanged. Checked structurally with `augment-provider-harness.mjs` and `filter-collection.mjs` (1 request for the feature).

```bash
node tests/e2e/api/runners/databricks-token-fixture.mjs &
INCLUDE_PREVIEW=1 make run-provider-harness-test PROVIDER=databricks FEATURE="databricks oauth scopes" BASE_URL=http://localhost:8081
```

Routes: the change is in how the key mints its token, so it applies the same way to `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, embeddings and `/v1/decisions` on Databricks keys. The harness case covers chat completions. No other provider reuses `DatabricksKeyConfig`.

## Open question

Databricks doesn't document which scope covers the Unity AI Gateway inference paths (`/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/...`). The docs tell users to test a scoped secret there or keep `all-apis`. Someone should confirm this against a real workspace.

data.title: feat(routing): add named model routers with a persisted table and config.json support
data.body:
## Overview

Adds named model routers. Until now Bifrost had a single complexity router, stored as two `governance_config` rows. A router is now a named complexity classifier with its own phrases and settings, stored in its own `model_routers` table. The existing config becomes the built-in `default` router, so gateways keep routing exactly as before.

## Changes

- **New `model_routers` table.** Each setting has its own column.
  - Phrase lists and criteria are JSON text columns.
  - The optional blocks (semantic, decision, llm, session, suggestions) are nullable columns anchored on one field each, so "block absent" stays distinct from "block present with zero values".
  - No column has a gorm default, because a zero is often a real setting (for example `min_similarity` 0).
  - A round-trip test fills every field by reflection, so a config field added without a column fails the test.
- **Store API.** `ConfigStore` gains `GetModelRouters`, `GetModelRouter`, `CreateModelRouter`, `UpdateModelRouter`, `DeleteModelRouter` and `ResetModelRouter`.
  - Ids may contain only letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 64 characters.
  - Names must be unique and at most 255 characters. "Default" is reserved for the default router.
  - The default router cannot be created or deleted.
  - Unreadable rows return `ErrConfigUnreadable`, and listing skips them with a warning.
- **The default router replaces the old singleton.** `GetComplexityAnalyzerConfig`, `UpdateComplexityAnalyzerConfig` and `ResetComplexityAnalyzerConfig` now read and write the `default` row. An unsaved default still reads as "nothing configured", so callers use the built-in defaults, and `GetGovernanceConfig` still serves the default router's config.
- **Saves keep bookkeeping.**
  - A save that omits the config.json section hashes, the name/description hash or the embedding fingerprint keeps the stored values. A dashboard save therefore never erases them.
  - Reset clears only the fingerprint.
  - Saves and resets run under a row lock. The default router has no row until first saved, so a placeholder row is inserted inside the transaction and overwritten before commit.
- **Migration `add_model_routers_table`.** It creates the table and moves the stored complexity config into the `default` row, carrying section hashes and the embedding fingerprint. The first boot therefore neither re-applies config.json over dashboard edits nor re-embeds phrases.
  - No stored config, or only half of one, creates no row.
  - An unreadable stored config is skipped with a warning, because reading it would have degraded to defaults before too.
  - The migration is non-rollbackable.
- **Rollback safety.** The legacy `governance_config` rows are left in place. Saving the default router rewrites them in the shapes older versions accept, so a rolled-back Bifrost still routes on the latest default config.
- **config.json.**
  - New top-level `model_routers` list, with the matching schema `$def`. The entry with id `default` configures the default router.
  - `governance.complexity_analyzer_config` is deprecated but still works. It is ignored with a warning when `model_routers` is present, and the two spellings are never merged field by field.
  - Reconciliation moved out of `mergeGovernanceConfig` into `loadModelRoutersConfig`, which runs after governance.
  - Split mode applies only the sections whose hash changed, plus name and description under their own hash. Dashboard edits survive reboots.
  - Source-of-truth mode reverts drift and deletes routers the file no longer declares. It never deletes the default router, and an invalid entry does not delete the router it names.
  - Duplicate ids and invalid entries are logged and skipped without blocking the other routers.
  - A router whose stored row is unreadable is replaced by its file declaration.
  - Without a config store, declared routers are kept in memory on `Config.ModelRouters`.
- **Design notes.** The tier boundaries stay as columns because the config API and config.json still accept them, even though nothing routes on them.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
# Core/Transports
go version
go test ./framework/configstore/... ./transports/bifrost-http/...

# UI
cd ui
pnpm i || npm i
pnpm test || npm test
pnpm build || npm run build
```

Manual checks:

1. Boot against a database that already has a saved complexity config. Confirm a `default` row appears in `model_routers` with the same phrases, hashes and fingerprint, that the `governance_config` rows are untouched, and that nothing is re-embedded.
2. Boot with only the deprecated `governance.complexity_analyzer_config` key. Behavior should be unchanged.
3. Add a top-level `model_routers` list to config.json, with a `default` entry and a second router such as:

   ```json
   {"model_routers": [{"id": "support", "name": "Support", "keywords": {"simple_keywords": ["..."], "medium_keywords": ["..."], "complex_keywords": ["..."]}}]}
   ```

   - Confirm the routers are created.
   - Edit a section in the dashboard and reboot with an unchanged file. The edit should survive.
   - Set `"source_of_truth": "config.json"` and remove an entry. That router should be deleted and `default` kept.

New config: the top-level `model_routers` array in config.json, documented in `transports/config.schema.json`.

## Screenshots/Recordings

N/A, no UI changes.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Existing config.json files and stored configs keep working. The deprecated `governance.complexity_analyzer_config` key is still honored.

## Related issues

N/A

## Security considerations

No new auth or secret handling. Router ids are restricted to a safe character set, since other stores key data by them.

## Checklist

- [ ] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [ ] I updated documentation where needed
- [ ] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)
- [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

data.title: fix(governance): start a newly added budget at zero when the operator resets usage
data.body:
## Summary

Adding a budget window on an edit copies the spend already counted in the closest shorter window into it, since that money was spent inside the new window too. That happened even when the operator chose **Reset Usage** on the same edit, so the new budget showed old spend while every edited budget went to zero.

- The new window now follows the same choice as the rest of the edit: it carries the spend over on **Preserve Usage**, and starts at zero on **Reset Usage**.
- Applies wherever the shared reconciler runs: customers, virtual key and model-config budgets, and owners in other builds that use it.
- The reset prompt's copy (all 11 locales) now says what each choice does: Reset Usage zeroes every budget the owner keeps, changed or not; Preserve Usage keeps the counters, and a newly added budget starts with the usage of the next shorter budget, if there is one.

## Tests

- `TestReconcileOwnedBudgetsNewWindowFollowsTheResetChoice`
- `transports/bifrost-http/handlers` and `lib` suites pass; i18n check clean.

data.title: feat(ui): manage model routers and model routing rules
data.body:
## Overview

The dashboard for named model routers (#9778) and model routing rules (#9781). The Complexity Router page becomes **Model Routers**:
- one tab lists the routers, another lists the model routing rules that send requests to them
- each router opens on its own configuration page, which is the former complexity-router page scoped to that router

`/workspace/complexity-router` redirects to the Default router and keeps its `tab`.

## Changes

- **Routers list.** Each row shows the router's classifier and model, its live status, pending phrase suggestions, and how many rules use it.
- **New router dialog.** The new router starts from the Default router: either a copy of it as it is now, or its classifier settings with the shipped phrases ("Start fresh"). A fresh router opens on the classifier choice; a copy opens ready to use. The gateway refuses empty phrase lists, so there is no empty start.
- **Router page** (`?router=<id>`). This is the existing configuration page with its steps, sheets and suggestions tab. It now reads and saves through the model router API, and adds:
  - a breadcrumb
  - Edit details (name and description)
  - Delete, which shows the gateway's 409 naming the rules that still use the router; the Default router cannot be deleted
  - the rules that send requests to the router
- **Model routing rules.**
  - The table and sheet follow the routing rule table and sheet: name, enabled, router, scope, priority and condition.
  - Targets are grouped by Simple, Medium and Complex, each with its own fallbacks and first-token timeout.
  - The condition builder leaves out `complexity_tier`, which the rule's router decides.
- **Shared code instead of copies.**
  - The target and fallback rows, the scope fields, the condition helpers, the rule actions menu and the delete dialog moved to `routing-rules/views/ruleShared.tsx`. Both rule sheets and both rule tables use them, and the routing rule test ids are unchanged.
  - `ClassifierChoice` and the new-router dialog share a `RadioCards` primitive.
- **Logs and dashboard.** New `model_router_ids` and `model_routing_rule_ids` filters. Log details show the router and the rule, each linking to their logs.
- **RBAC.** The pages and the nav item are gated on Governance, which is what the model router APIs enforce. The complexity-router page used to check RoutingRules.
- **Helm.**
  - New values `bifrost.modelRouters` and `bifrost.modelRoutingRules`, rendered as `model_routers` and `model_routing_rules`, with schema, docs, template tests and a README Upcoming entry.
  - `bifrost.governance.complexityAnalyzerConfig.suggestions` is now allowed; the chart's schema rejected it.
- **OpenAPI.** The model routing log filters and log fields.
- **i18n.** Strings in all 11 locales. The tier and classifier names reuse each locale's existing terms.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [x] UI (React)
- [x] Docs

## How to test

```sh
cd ui
npm run typecheck
npx vitest run app/workspace/model-routers app/workspace/routing-rules components/filters
npm run i18n:check
npm run build

# Helm
helm lint helm-charts/bifrost
bash .github/workflows/scripts/validate-helm-templates.sh
```

E2E: `tests/e2e/features/model-routers/` is new, and `features/complexity-router/` now uses the model router endpoints and covers the old-URL redirect.

Manual checks:

data.body:
## Overview

Adds model routing rules, so requests can be routed by the tier of any named model router (from the previous PR), not only the default one. A model routing rule is a separate routing step: it runs after routing rules and before the virtual key allowlist and load balancing, so both of those see the model it picks. The first rule that matches names a router, the router classifies the request into SIMPLE, MEDIUM or COMPLEX, and that tier's target replaces the provider and model.

With no model routing rules saved, the step returns at once. In a parallel benchmark it costs the same per request as the routing rules gate: about 1.4 ns with no allocations.

## Changes

- **New tables `model_routing_rules` and `model_routing_targets`**, with migration `add_model_routing_rules_tables`. Like routing rules, a rule has a scope (global, team, customer, virtual key, user), an optional CEL condition and a priority. It also names a model router and has weighted targets per tier, each with its own provider, model, key, TTFT timeout and fallbacks.
  - Priorities are unique within a scope, in their own priority space, separate from routing rule priorities.
  - A rule's condition cannot use `complexity_tier`, because its router decides the tier only after the rule matches.
  - Like routing rules, a rule also stores the dashboard's condition builder state (`query`). It is never evaluated. An add-column migration step covers databases created before the column existed.
  - A router that rules still name cannot be deleted. The API returns 409 listing those rules. The router row is locked on both sides, so a rule saved at the same moment cannot be left naming a deleted router.
- **Routing step (`plugins/routing/modelrouting.go`).**
  - Only the first rule that matches counts; rules do not chain.
  - A tier without a target keeps the request's model.
  - A provider change clears a key that the routing rules pinned, unless the target pins its own key.
  - A target's fallbacks replace the request's chain only when the target has fallbacks. A fallback that omits its model keeps the incoming model, as for routing rules.
  - Large payloads skip the step.
- **Per-router runtime (`plugins/routing/modelrouters.go`).**
  - Each router owns its own semantic and LLM classifiers, embeddings, session state and tool-continuation tier.
  - The default router is a view over the plugin's existing fields, so it behaves as the single complexity router did, and it keeps the existing KV keys. Session state in flight survives the upgrade.
  - Each router classifies at most once per request. A routing rule's `complexity_tier` still classifies with the default router.
- **Rule cache (`plugins/routing/rules/modelrules.go`)** is built like the routing rules' `LocalStore`: a `sync.Map` from scope to an immutable slice, read without a lock. The weighted target pick is shared with routing rules (`pickWeighted`), and fallback resolution is shared with routing rules (`resolveRuleFallbacks`).
- **HTTP API:**
  - `/api/routing/model-routers`, plus `/{id}`, `/reset`, `/status` and `/status/retry`
  - `/api/routing/model-routing-rules` and `/{id}`
  - Model routing rules are gated on the `Governance` permissions, like model routers.
- **config.json.** New top-level `model_routing_rules` section, with JSON schema `$defs`.
  - Each rule is hashed as one unit, like routing rules.
  - In source-of-truth mode, rules the file drops are pruned before routers. A router that a kept rule moves off is pruned once the rules have synced.
- **Logs.** New columns `model_router_id/name` and `model_routing_rule_id/name`, with partial indexes. The filters `model_router_ids` and `model_routing_rule_ids` work in the logs API and the warp tools.

data.body:
## Overview

Adds the management API for the semantic complexity router's phrase suggestions. Suggestion runs already cluster sampled traffic and ask a model for new routing phrases. Until now there was no way to review the results, try a phrase, or start a run by hand. This PR adds those endpoints and documents the `suggestions` config block in the OpenAPI spec.

## Changes

- New endpoints under `/api/routing/complexity-suggestions`:
  - `GET /api/routing/complexity-suggestions` lists stored suggestions, largest cluster first. It filters by `?status=` (comma-separated, default `open`) and returns per-status counts, whether suggestions are enabled, the last run, and the next scheduled run time.
  - `GET /api/routing/complexity-suggestions/{suggestion_id}` returns one suggestion with the text of its example requests. Text is read from logs within the caller's access scope. A log that was deleted, hides its content, or is out of scope is listed without text.
  - `PUT /api/routing/complexity-suggestions/{suggestion_id}/status` accepts, dismisses, or reopens a suggestion. An open suggestion can be accepted or dismissed, and either can be reopened. `superseded` is set only by runs, so a superseded suggestion cannot be changed here (409).
  - `POST /api/routing/complexity-suggestions/test` routes example requests by nearest phrase against the serving phrase bank, and again against the bank with the given phrases added, without saving anything. It reports each example's tier before and after and whether it changed. It also reports each tested phrase's nearest existing phrase, which shows near-duplicates, and the share of examples the new phrases take over.
  - `GET /api/routing/complexity-suggestions/runs` lists runs newest first, with `?limit=` from 1 to 200 (default 20).
  - `POST /api/routing/complexity-suggestions/runs` starts a run outside the schedule and returns 202 with the run ID. It returns 409 if suggestions are off or a run is already queued or running.
- The complexity analyzer status endpoint now returns `suggestion_default_instructions`, the editable half of the shipped suggestion instructions, so a config client can seed an editor and offer a reset.
- The OpenAPI spec documents the `suggestions` config block (sampling, lookback, schedule, clustering limits, suggestion model, instructions) wherever the analyzer config appears, plus the new paths and schemas.
- Design decisions:
  - Accepted and dismissed decisions stick across runs. The status update rewrites the row whole, keeping its centroid, so the next run can still match the cluster and spends no model call on it.
  - Phrase testing applies the router's own `min_similarity` floor. `SuggestionSpace` now exposes it as `MinSimilarity`, so the "accepted" flag matches real routing.
  - Clients send phrase text and a tier, never a vector. The gateway embeds them, and tiers are read case-insensitively.
  - A phrase test is limited to 10 phrases and 32 examples.
  - Starting a run now reports whether a job was actually queued. A duplicate-job error counts as "not started", which lets the manual start return a proper conflict. Scheduled runs behave as before.
- The endpoints return 503 when there is no log store or the routing plugin is not loaded. The test endpoint returns 502 when the embedding provider fails.

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)

- [x] Plugins

Run the Go tests for the touched packages, then exercise the endpoints against a gateway with a log store and `suggestions.enabled: true` in the complexity analyzer config.

```sh
go version
go test ./plugins/routing/... ./transports/bifrost-http/...

# Manually
# List open suggestions, then include other statuses
curl -s localhost:8080/api/routing/complexity-suggestions
curl -s "localhost:8080/api/routing/complexity-suggestions?status=open,dismissed"

# Start a run now (expect 202 with run_id; a second call while it is in flight returns 409)
curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/routing/complexity-suggestions/runs

# Try a phrase against a suggestion's examples
curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/routing/complexity-suggestions/test \
  -d '{"phrases":[{"tier":"SIMPLE","text":"where is my refund"}],"suggestion_id":"<id>"}'

curl -s -X PUT localhost:8080/api/routing/complexity-suggestions/<id>/status -d '{"status":"accepted"}'
```

data.title: feat(complexity router): scope phrase suggestions to a model router
data.body:
## Overview

Phrase suggestions for the complexity router now belong to a specific model router instead of being gateway-wide. Today a gateway has one router, `default`, so behavior is unchanged. The scoping, versioning and run-sizing needed to support several routers are now in place.

This PR also adds a "Run now" flow that lets operators pick how much traffic a run reads and see what it will cost before starting it. Previously the button started a run over the entire lookback with no preview.

## Changes

- **Router scoping**
  - Suggestions and runs are stamped with `router_id` and `router_version`.
  - Listing, reading, status updates, phrase testing, run history, run start and run pruning are all scoped to one router.
  - Another router's suggestions are not listed, matched, superseded or reachable by ID (404).
  - Every suggestion endpoint takes `?router_id=`, defaulting to `default`. An unknown router returns 404.
  - Manual and scheduled runs for a router are queued under a per-router partition, so one router's run never blocks another's. The inline (no job runner) guard is also per router.
  - Scheduled run IDs now include the router ID.
- **Staleness**
  - A suggestion records the phrase bank version it was computed against. The version is currently the serving generation's fingerprint, standing in until routers carry their own.
  - Suggestions and the list response now include `router_version` and a `stale` flag. The UI shows an "Earlier phrase bank" badge on stale suggestions, advising the operator to test them against current phrases.
- **Run windows**
  - `POST /api/routing/complexity-suggestions/runs?window=24h|7d|…` reads only part of the lookback.
  - A run records its `window_start`.
  - A window that is malformed, non-positive or longer than the lookback returns 400.
- **Run estimate**
  - New `GET /api/routing/complexity-suggestions/runs/estimate` sizes a run without starting it. It returns the captured requests in the window, how many would be clustered, assigned or skipped, and the maximum number of suggestion-model calls.
  - Only captured timestamps are read, via a new `CountCaptured`, so no vectors are fetched.
  - The model-call bound assumes every cluster is the smallest one kept, so it is an upper limit.
  - It returns 409 when suggestions are off and 503 when there is no warmed phrase bank.
- **Pluggable traffic source**
  - A run reads its requests through a `Traffic` interface. It defaults to scanning the space's captured requests, which is one router's traffic while a gateway has one router.
  - With several routers, requests can instead be selected from the logs by router.
- **Capture namespaces**
  - Capture cleanup no longer deletes embedding spaces that another serving router still writes to. `SetLiveNamespaces` supplies the spaces to keep. With one router the default is unchanged.
- **Log store**
  - `ListComplexitySuggestionRuns` takes a `ComplexitySuggestionRunFilter` (router and IDs).
  - `PruneComplexitySuggestionRuns` prunes per router.
  - New `DeleteComplexityRouterSuggestions` removes a deleted router's suggestions and runs. It runs in a transaction on RDB stores. ClickHouse has no transaction, so a failure on the second delete leaves the runs behind and a retry removes them.
  - The Hybrid and ClickHouse stores are updated to match.
- **UI**
  - "Run now" opens a dialog with a window selector. Only windows that fit the configured lookback are offered, and it defaults to 7 days.
  - The dialog shows a live estimate of requests, clustering and maximum model calls.
  - The suggestions tab, example loading, status changes and phrase testing pass the suggestion's router ID.
  - New strings are added to all locales, including plural forms for Russian.
- **Docs**
  - The OpenAPI spec is updated for the new parameters, response fields, the 400 and 404 responses, and the estimate endpoint.

- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

- [x] Transports (HTTP)

- [x] UI (React)

## How to test

```sh

go version
go test ./framework/logstore/... ./plugins/routing/... ./transports/bifrost-http/handlers/...

# UI
cd ui
pnpm i || npm i
pnpm test || npm test
pnpm build || npm run build
```

1. Open the complexity router's Suggestions tab. Suggestions computed against an earlier phrase bank show an "Earlier phrase bank" badge.
2. Click "Run now". The dialog offers only windows within the lookback and shows the request count and the maximum number of model calls. Changing the window refreshes the estimate.
3. Start a run with a 24h window. `POST .../runs?window=24h` returns 202 and the run's `window_start` is 24 hours before its start.

6. Call `GET .../runs/estimate?window=7d`. The response should contain `requests`, `clustered`, `assigned`, `skipped` and `max_model_calls`.

data.title: feat(complexity router): run phrase suggestions on a schedule
data.body:
## Overview

Adds scheduled phrase-suggestion runs to the complexity router. A run reads the requests captured in the lookback window, clusters a sample of them, asks the suggestion model about each cluster, and reconciles the answers with the suggestions already stored. This is what lets the job repeat on a schedule without duplicating suggestions or overriding user decisions.

## Changes

- **Reading captured traffic**
  - `EachCaptured` pages captured request vectors for a time window out of the vector store. Both ends of the window are inclusive, since capture times are whole seconds.
  - `SuggestionSpace` snapshots the serving generation: its phrase bank with vectors, the capture namespace, and the embedding function. It holds the generation until `Close`, so a reload mid-run can't change what the run reads.
  - `ErrNoServingGeneration` is returned when the classifier is off, warming, or failed.
- **Clustering past the budget**
  - `Clusterer.Assign` counts requests into the clusters already found without forming new ones. Requests that match no cluster are reported as unmatched.
  - Cost is one dot product per cluster per request, with no extra vector retained.
  - A run clusters a reservoir sample of the window, then assigns the rest, up to 10× the sample size. Suggestion counts therefore cover the whole window, not just the sample.
- **Request text comes from the logs, not the vector store**
  - Captured vectors are stored without their text.
  - `LoggedInputText` rebuilds the text the classifier embedded from a log's input history (chat or Responses shape) and user agent, so the same harness clean-up (e.g. stripping Claude Code's `<system-reminder>` blocks) applies.
  - The new `Options.Texts` hook in `suggest` fetches text only for the members shown to the model. Members it can't read are dropped.
  - A cluster with no readable examples gets the new `unreadable` category and is never sent to the model.
- **Reconciliation (`suggestrun`)**
  - Clusters are matched to stored suggestions by centroid similarity (≥ 0.85), heaviest cluster first.
  - Accepted and dismissed suggestions are left untouched and cost no model call, so a decision sticks.
  - Open suggestions are refreshed in place.
  - Open suggestions that lost their traffic, whose cluster is now covered, or whose embedding space is no longer served are superseded.
  - New clusters become new open suggestions.
  - Run records are written at start and finish. A cancelled run is still recorded as finished, using a detached context. Only the 200 most recent run records are kept.
  - The model is called for at most 200 clusters per run, heaviest first.
- **Partial failure**
  - A failed model call for one cluster doesn't fail the run. That cluster is retried next run, and the failure is noted on the run record.
  - The run fails only if every cluster fails, or if there is no model.
- **Scheduling (routing plugin)**
  - Every node checks once a minute whether the schedule's latest slot has a run.
  - The slot is derived from the calendar, so all nodes agree on it. Runs are queued as a sidekiq job keyed by the slot ID, so nodes queue one job between them.
  - A node without a job runner runs the slot itself, guarded against overlap.
  - Scheduling waits while the semantic router is still warming, rather than recording a failed run for the slot.
  - The model call reuses the LLM fallback classifier's internal chat path (including the Responses API retry) and totals the cost of its calls into the run record.
  - The model defaults to the suggestions block's provider and model, falling back to the `llm` block.
- **Server wiring**
  - Request text is read via `FindByID`, which also covers payloads offloaded to object storage.
  - Registers the `complexity_suggestions` sidekiq job kind.
  - Wiring now lives in `wireRoutingSuggestions`, called from both Bootstrap and `ReloadPlugin`. Previously a reloaded routing plugin would have come up without log retention, delete recording, or the suggestion store.
- **Shutdown**
  - Plugin cleanup stops suggestion runs before closing the classifier, since a run holds its serving space.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [x] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

Run the Go tests for the routing plugin and the HTTP server:

```sh
go version
go test ./plugins/routing/... ./transports/bifrost-http/server/...
```

Expected outcomes:

- `TestRunCreatesRefreshesAndSupersedes`: over three runs, suggestions are created, a dismissed one stays dismissed with no model call, an open one is refreshed in place, and one whose traffic left the window is superseded.
- `TestRunCountsTheWholeWindowPastTheBudget`: with a window larger than the cluster budget, the sample is clustered and the remaining requests are assigned, so counts cover all 80 requests.
- `TestRunFailures`: one failed cluster leaves the run succeeded with a note, while all clusters failing, or no model, fails the run and records the failure.
- `TestSuggestReadsTextsOnlyForShownMembers`: text is fetched only for the representatives, an unreadable member is dropped, and an all-unreadable cluster never reaches the model.
- `TestComplexitySuggestionsRunsADueSlotOnce` and `TestComplexitySuggestionsQueuesDueSlots`: a due slot runs or queues exactly once, and a run in flight is not queued again.
- `TestComplexitySuggestionTextsReadsWhatTheRouterEmbedded`: request text comes back as the router embedded it, and is never returned for a deleted or content-hidden log.

No new configuration is introduced. Runs use the existing `suggestions` block (`enabled`, `lookback_days`, `max_clustered_requests`, `min_cluster_requests`, `provider`, `model`, `instructions`, schedule) and fall back to the `llm` block for the model and guidance.

data.title: feat(governance): add a business unit owner column to budgets
data.body:
## Summary

Lets a business unit hold one budget per reset window, the way a team or customer does.

- `governance_budgets.business_unit_id` owner column, added by migration `add_budget_business_unit_id_column`. Index only, no foreign key: the config loader may write a budget naming a business unit before any row for that unit exists. The index is its own migration, `add_budget_business_unit_id_index`, following the other index migrations: no transaction, built with `ensureIndexConcurrently` (concurrent on Postgres, replacing an INVALID leftover) and rolled back with `dropIndexConcurrently`. A fresh install gets the same index name from the struct tag.
- The column joins the one-owner check in `TableBudget.BeforeSave`.
- `UpdateBudget` keeps a stored business unit owner when the write names no owner at all. Without this, editing a budget's limits without restating who holds it nulled the owner and the unit silently stopped being capped. A write that names an owner is an ownership change and is applied as given.
- Config loader: a `governance.budgets[]` row naming a business unit is written directly, and skipped while an access profile governs the unit, as a team's or customer's is. `config.schema.json` documents `business_unit_id` on budgets and `budgets[]` / `calendar_aligned` on business units.
- `BusinessUnitGovernance` carries `BudgetIDs` instead of a single id.

`GenerateBudgetHash` never covered owner columns, so no budget is rewritten on the first boot after upgrade.

## Tests

- `TestMigrationAddBudgetBusinessUnitIDColumn`, `TestMigrationAddBudgetBusinessUnitIDIndex` (SQLite, and Postgres when the local test server is reachable), `TestBudgetTagsBuildBusinessUnitIDIndex`
- `TestTableBudgetBeforeSaveCountsTheBusinessUnitOwner`
- `TestUpdateBudgetKeepsTheBusinessUnitOwnerOnAnOwnerlessWrite`
- `framework/configstore`, `plugins/governance`, `transports/bifrost-http/{handlers,lib}` suites pass on this branch alone.

data.title: feat(complexity router): add schedule, budget and model settings for phrase suggestions
data.body:
## Overview

Adds run settings to the complexity router's phrase-suggestions config. Until now the block only controlled traffic capture (`enabled`, `sample_rate`, `lookback_days`). It now also controls when suggestion runs start, how much traffic each run clusters, which model writes the phrases, and what instructions that model gets.

## Changes

- **Schedule**
  - New `schedule` object with `every`, `at`, `weekday` and `timezone`. `every` uses the budget-reset style: `6h`, `1d` or `1w`.
  - Defaults to daily at 03:00 UTC.
  - Hourly intervals must divide a day and start at midnight. Daily intervals go up to 30d, weekly up to 4w.
  - `at` is rejected on hourly schedules, and `weekday` is rejected on non-weekly ones.
  - `LastSlot` and `NextSlot` compute the most recent and next start times.
  - Slots are aligned to the calendar, not to when the schedule was saved. For example, `2d` runs on days whose number since 1970-01-01 is even in the schedule's timezone. Every node therefore computes the same slot without shared state.
  - Times are wall-clock in the configured zone, so a 03:00 run stays at 03:00 across daylight-saving changes. A time the change skips runs at the next valid time.
- **Run settings**
  - `max_clustered_requests` bounds how many requests one run clusters (default 20000, range 1000–100000). The rest of the window is assigned to the clusters found, so counts still cover all of it. The default and ceiling come from measured clustering time and vector memory.
  - `min_cluster_requests` is the smallest cluster that gets a suggestion (default 6, range 2–1000).
  - `provider` and `model` select the suggestion model. They must be set together; leaving both empty uses the llm fallback block's model.
  - `instructions` replaces the shipped suggestion instructions (max 8000 characters). Tier definitions and the fixed reinforcement are still added. Blank instructions are normalized to empty, which means the shipped ones.
- **Strict decoding**
  - The suggestions block and the schedule both reject unknown fields, so a misspelled setting can't be silently ignored.
  - Defaults are filled in on normalization, so stored configs now include them.
  - `EffectiveSchedule()` returns the schedule with defaults applied.
- **Schema and types**
  - `config.schema.json` gains the new fields, a `complexity_suggestions_schedule` definition, and `dependentRequired` between `provider` and `model`.
  - The UI types gain `SuggestionsSchedule` and the new `SuggestionsConfig` fields.
  - There is no UI form yet; the settings are edited through `config.json` and the API.
- **Tests**
  - New tests cover slot computation, including a daylight-saving transition and alternate weeks across a year boundary.
  - Config tests cover strict decoding, defaults and out-of-range values.
  - A test in the suggest package checks that its instruction limit matches the config limit, so the config can't save instructions that a run would then refuse.
  - Validator tests check the schema against the new settings.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [x] Plugins
- [x] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
# Core/Transports
go version
go test ./framework/configstore/... ./plugins/routing/complexity/... ./transports/bifrost-http/lib/...

# UI
cd ui
pnpm i || npm i
pnpm test || npm test
pnpm build || npm run build
```

To try the new settings, add this to the complexity analyzer config:

```json
"suggestions": {
  "enabled": true,
  "schedule": { "every": "1w", "at": "04:30", "weekday": "friday", "timezone": "Europe/Berlin" },
  "max_clustered_requests": 5000,
  "min_cluster_requests": 10,
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-5",
  "instructions": "be brief"
}
```

Expected results:
- The config loads, and omitted fields read back with their defaults (daily, 03:00, UTC, 20000, 6).
- `"every": "24h"`, `"at": "3:00"`, an unknown schedule key such as `cron`, a `provider` without a `model`, or `max_clustered_requests` below 1000 are all rejected.

## Screenshots/Recordings

Not applicable. The UI change is type definitions only.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

All new fields are optional and take defaults. Existing configs keep working, and stored suggestion blocks gain default values for the new fields the next time they are normalized.

N/A

## Security considerations

- Instructions are capped at 8000 characters. The shipped tier definitions and fixed reinforcement are always appended, so custom instructions replace only the editable part.
- Run size is bounded (at most 100000 clustered requests, about 600 MB of vectors at 1536 dimensions), which limits memory use per run.
- Unknown fields are rejected in both the config and the schema.

data.title: feat(routing): classify statements with a model router to test its tiers
data.body:
## Overview

Adds `POST /api/routing/model-routers/{router_id}/classify`, which classifies a page of statements with a model router as it is served now and returns the complexity tier each one gets. This lets you check a router's configuration (exemplars, `min_similarity`, decision model, fallbacks) against a labelled dataset before live traffic depends on it.

## Changes

- New endpoint takes up to 100 statements per call. Each has optional `id`, `previous_user_messages` and `expected_tier` (case-insensitive, SIMPLE/MEDIUM/COMPLEX). Results come back in input order.
- Each statement is wrapped as the latest user turn of a chat request. It then goes through the same input extraction, classifier and fallback chain as live traffic.
- Nothing is saved. Each statement runs on its own context with an empty request ID and no session ID, so no session tier is read or moved and the statement is not captured for phrase suggestions.
- Each result includes the tier (omitted if none), the mechanism (`semantic`, `decision`, `llm` or `skipped`), the score or confidence, the matched exemplar, the answering model and the routing engine trace.
- When a semantic match is rejected for falling below `min_similarity`, the nearest exemplar is now reported as `semantic_miss`. It is kept even when the decision model or LLM classifier then answers. This is how you tell whether to add exemplars or lower the threshold.
- The response aggregates the page: per-tier counts (with `UNCLASSIFIED`), labelled and correct counts, accuracy, and a confusion matrix keyed by expected tier then given tier. Accuracy and the matrix are omitted when nothing is labelled.
- Limits: 1–100 inputs per call and 32 KiB per statement (previous turns included). Eight statements are classified concurrently, with a 60s backstop per statement.
- Request bodies are decoded strictly, so a misspelled field such as `expected_teir` returns 400 instead of being dropped. The existing strict decoder from the model router handlers was extracted into a shared `decodeStrictJSON` helper for this.
- Status codes: 404 for an unknown router, 400 for invalid input, and 503 when the routing plugin is not loaded.
- A decision-model router, or one that falls back to the decision model or LLM classifier, makes one billed model call per statement that reaches it.
- Added OpenAPI paths and schemas for the endpoint, with a request example and the required `Governance:Create` permission.
- Added unit tests for the plugin and handler, plus an e2e collection case. The e2e case creates a temporary decision-model router, classifies a labelled page, checks the response contract and refusals, and deletes the router on every path.

## Type of change

- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)

- [x] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [x] Docs

## How to test

Run the new unit tests, then exercise the endpoint against a running gateway.

```sh

go version
go test ./...

# Targeted
go test ./plugins/routing/... -run ClassifyWithModelRouter
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/handlers/... -run ClassifyWithModelRouter

# UI
cd ui
pnpm i || npm i
pnpm test || npm test
pnpm build || npm run build
```

Manual check:

```sh
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/routing/model-routers/default/classify" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"inputs":[{"id":"row-1","text":"what time is it in Tokyo?","expected_tier":"SIMPLE"}]}'
```

Expected: 200 with one result per input in order, and an aggregate block with tier counts, accuracy and the confusion matrix. An unknown router returns 404. A bad `expected_tier`, an unknown field, an empty page, or more than 100 inputs returns 400.

No new configs or environment variables.

## Screenshots/Recordings

- [x] No

## Security considerations

- The endpoint requires `Governance:Create` (RBAC role or API key scope) and uses the same management auth as the other routing endpoints.
- Calls can trigger paid model calls, so page size (100), statement size (32 KiB) and concurrency (8) are bounded.
- Test statements are never captured or tied to a session, so they cannot affect live routing state or phrase suggestions.

data.title: feat(complexity router): improve phrase suggestion clustering and template handling
data.body:
## Overview

Complexity-router suggestions now handle traffic that is one prompt template sent over and over with different fills (agent scaffolds, "write an image prompt" setups, role-play preambles). Before, the suggestion was written from a single representative request, so its phrase often copied that request's own fill. Clustering also let small request types get absorbed into a larger neighbour's cluster, or dropped as fragments below the minimum size.

This PR adds a `template` suggestion category, stops phrases from copying one request's own material, and makes clustering better at keeping small request types separate.

## Changes

- **New `template` suggestion category**
  - It is actionable and shown in the UI filter menu, with its own label and description.
  - It replaces the usual `uncovered`/`weak`/`misrouted`/`mixed` label whenever a template is detected. The suggestion is worth making whatever today's routing is, and the label tells the reviewer why the phrase reads like the template's opening.
  - The `category` enum is extended in the OpenAPI schema and generated JSON, the UI types, and the category counts. The label and description are translated in all supported locales.
- **Template detection**
  - The suggester looks for an opening shared by the example requests: at least 6 words, shared by at least 3 distinct requests, and not just one request repeated.
  - When found, it is stored on the suggestion as `Template`, and the LLM is told which wording is fixed and not to copy the parts that change.
- **Pasted-material guard**
  - In a template cluster, a phrase that copies a run of more than 8 words from the fill of exactly one request is treated as a leak. It gets the same feedback, retry and fallback handling as other leaked phrases, including the sanitized fallback path.
  - Outside template clusters nothing is refused, because a phrase is meant to be a minimal edit of one request there.
- **Cluster splitting**
  - A finished cluster is tried as two groups using spherical 2-means.
  - The split stands only if the group centres are less similar than `SplitSimilarity` (defaults to the join threshold; negative disables), both halves reach `MinRequests`, and each has at least 2 members.
  - Only clusters that kept every member are split, since larger clusters' sums include vectors that are gone. Halves are retried, so a cluster holding three types can come apart.
  - This undoes absorption, where a small type was handed a neighbouring type's phrase and tier.
- **Fragment rescue**
  - Clusters too small to keep are merged with each other at `RescueSimilarity` (default 0.75; negative disables) before being dropped. A type that k-means split into several tiny pieces now gets a cluster.
  - Fragments are never merged into a cluster that is already big enough, which would give them a neighbour's phrase.
- **Eval tool (`complexitysuggesteval`)**
  - New flags: `-split`, `-rescue`, and `-drop-below`, which leaves suggestions covering too small a share of their own cluster out of scoring.
  - Labelled input can carry an `intent` field. The run then prints a purity report: types with their own cluster, absorbed, absorbed cross-tier, dropped, and member purity. Cross-tier cases are listed as examples.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [x] Plugins
- [x] UI (React)
- [x] Docs

## How to test

```sh
# Core/Plugins
go test ./plugins/routing/complexity/suggest/...

# UI
cd ui
pnpm i || npm i
pnpm test || npm test
pnpm build || npm run build
```

Expected results:

- `TestSharedTemplate` and `TestPastedFrom` cover detection, short instructions, too few requests, repeated requests, and the paste check.
- `TestSuggestTemplateCluster` covers a pasted fill being refused and retried, and the result being categorised as `template`.
- `TestClustererSplitsTwoTypesInOneCluster` and `TestClustererRescuesFragmentsOfSmallTypes` cover the split and rescue behaviour, including that a negative value disables each.
- The UI suggestions test expects `template: 0` in the category counts.

To check clustering on labelled data, run `complexitysuggesteval` with `-cluster-only` on a JSONL file whose items include an `intent` field. Compare the printed purity line with `-split -1 -rescue -1` against the defaults.

New configuration (all optional):

- `ClusterOptions.SplitSimilarity`: 0 uses the join threshold, negative disables.
- `ClusterOptions.RescueSimilarity`: 0 uses 0.75, negative disables.

## Screenshots/Recordings

The suggestions filter menu gains a "Prompt template" entry, and suggestion cards show the new category label and description. Screenshots to be added.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

API clients that validate the suggestion `category` against a strict enum will need to accept the new `template` value.

N/A

## Security considerations

None beyond the existing leak filtering. The pasted-material guard further reduces the chance that one request's own content ends up in a suggested phrase.
